standards.name: MISRA C++:2008
standards.reason: No compliance checker covers the full rule set, and no rule-by-rule deviation and approval record exists; the local coding rules and the clang-tidy subset cannot replace a formal assessment.

standards.name: AUTOSAR C++14
standards.reason: No clause-by-clause conformance matrix, tool qualification, or external audit has been performed; support for AUTOSAR type aliases does not mean compliance with the AUTOSAR C++14 coding guidelines.

rules.claim: Core libraries disable exceptions and RTTI; the established hot paths after Prepare()/Start() do not allocate, and out-of-memory behavior is explicit.
rules.limit: Configuration-time assertions check COMPILE_OPTIONS on the four core targets; consumers and external dependencies are outside this proof. Allocation sentinels cover only executed hot paths, and the explicit out-of-memory policy still requires code review.

rules.claim: Publication uses the in-place BeginWrite/CommitWrite/AbortWrite slot protocol and preserves each container's abort semantics.
rules.limit: Tests cover the registered protocol and equivalence cases; whether new call sites follow single-producer and pairing discipline still requires review.

rules.claim: Hot paths use counters and rate-limited logging rather than unconditional per-message formatting; the logging hot path does not allocate.
rules.limit: Tests prove rate limiting and zero allocation on the selected logging paths; no static checker proves that every new call site avoids per-message logging.
